problem: Given that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ evaluate ${f}_{yxx}(1,1)$ if ${f}_{xy}(x,y)=y{e}^{xy}(2+xy).$
worked_solution:
As the higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. Hence, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yxx}(x,y) & ={f}_{xyx}(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{xy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{xy}(2+xy)) \\  & ={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}(2+xy)+{y}^{2}{e}^{xy} \\  & ={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}(3+xy).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,1):$

$$
{f}_{yxx}(1,1)=(1)^{2}{e}^{1\cdot 1}(3+(1)(1))=4e\,\,
$$
